deviations: Ambiguity resolution machinery invented (vision 06 §1 names 'the stricter matching class' without an ordering): documented STRICTNESS rank H1(10)>H2(9)>H3(8)>H5(7)>H4(6)>H6(5)>H7(4) — money first, persistent credential mutations next, account lifecycle above login, then device-data flows — with H8 ranked last and resolved RESIDUALLY (H8 claims an action only when no more specific class matches). Rationale encoded in code: the gate's trust grant follows the resolved class, so the narrower class is the conservative resolution; resolving ambiguity to H8 would grant the broadest trust from the weakest signal. The phase doc's canonical case (ambiguous checkout-like form -> H1) is a pinned matrix row.

H3/H4/H8 overlap reconciled (all three detection rows literally fire on a password field): H3's ENTRY detection is scoped to create/change cues (new/confirm/current/reset password wording); a bare secret field with no cues routes to H8 — the vision's own wrong-site/injected-capture class — and a login-shaped secret (identifier+secret pair) routes to H4. All three are subsets of the vision's literal 'type=password fields (entry)' detection; each gates identically, only the card label and trust key differ. Lone-secret SUBMISSION with no cues still fails to H3 (no fail-open). Recorded as an interpretation, not a vision change.

Pair-based H4 breadth: submitting over any identifier+secret pair gates as H4 even without login wording (fail-to-confirm); identifier/secret TYPING while the complementary member exists on the page gates too. This can over-gate an unrelated submit on a page that embeds a login widget — the safe direction, documented at the code site.

ART-4 query guard: purchase context reads host+path only (query/fragment stripped before matching), and purchase verbs on NAV_LINKS candidates additionally require host/path corroboration — a search-results link titled 'Buy apple pie online' stays ungated while a 'Buy now' button gates anywhere. Both are pinned matrix rows.

Entry-shape heuristics: TAP-focus on an editable field is treated as credential entry when the field is a secret (typing would follow); typing a card-number-shaped value (12–19 grouped digits) into ANY field gates H1 as a content-shape exfil guard. Typed values are otherwise never fingerprinted and never rendered on a GateCard.

TaskGate deny-key granularity is (class, site): the phase doc's REQUEST event carries exactly (class, site), so 'same action denied twice' is enforced at that granularity (two different H2 buttons denied on one site = two refusals = abort). TIMEOUT(30s) is a first-class event decided exactly like DENY; the TIMEOUT_SECONDS constant lives in TaskGate (ART-5) while the timer lives with the UI (phase doc §6).

PageContext.site = URL host minus a leading 'www.' — v1 heuristic without public-suffix resolution (login.example.co.uk stays login.example.co.uk); sufficient for the trust key and card display; revisit only if a real site family splits it.
